10-6.solution: Let the work take \(t\) days; X works \(t - 5\) of them. \(\frac{t - 5}{20} + \frac{t}{30} = 1\) gives \(3(t - 5) + 2t = 60\), so \(t = 15\) days.

10-15.solution: Net filling rate \(= \frac{1}{6} + \frac{1}{9} - \frac{1}{18} = \frac{3 + 2 - 1}{18} = \frac{2}{9}\) of the tank an hour, so \(4.5\) hours.

10-21.solution: A works at \(\frac{3}{4} \div 12 = \frac{1}{16}\) a day and B at \(\frac{1}{2} \div 8 = \frac{1}{16}\). Together \(\frac{1}{8}\), so \(8\) days.

10-24.solution: Their efficiencies are \(2 : 3\), so the faster does \(\frac{3}{5}\) of the joint rate \(\frac{1}{15}\): \(\frac{1}{25}\) a day, \(25\) days alone.

10-25.solution: Net filling rate \(= \frac{1}{4} + \frac{1}{6} - \frac{1}{12} = \frac{3 + 2 - 1}{12} = \frac{1}{3}\) of the tank an hour, so \(3\) hours.

10-28.solution: The trench is \(10 \times 8 = 80\) worker-days. In 3 days \(30\) are done, leaving \(50\) for the last 5 days: \(10\) workers. With 6 left, \(4\) more are needed.

10-29.solution: Together they do \(\frac{40\%}{4} = 10\%\) a day and A does \(\frac{60\%}{9} = 6\frac{2}{3}\%\), so B does \(3\frac{1}{3}\%\) a day: \(30\) days.
